title: Design System: Outlook Local AI Chat

title.purpose: The selected email subject, inherited from the Windows message-box font and enlarged relative to the user's system setting.

body.purpose: Transcript, composer, settings fields, and other primary reading text.

label.purpose: Speaker names, settings labels, and the primary action.

hint.purpose: Metadata, disclosures, keyboard hints, and operational status without falling below the implementation's 8pt floor.

components.name: Primary AI Action
components.description: Starts the bounded AI request and changes to Cancel while that request is active.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { min-width: 104px; height: 80px; border: 1px solid #005fb8; border-radius: 0; background: #005fb8; color: HighlightText; padding: 0 16px; font: 700 9pt system-ui, sans-serif; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: #004f99; } .ds-btn-primary:active { background: #003f7a; } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid Highlight; outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-btn-primary:disabled { opacity: 0.55; } @media (forced-colors: active) { .ds-btn-primary { border-color: ButtonText; background: Highlight; color: HighlightText; forced-color-adjust: auto; } }

components.name: Draft Action
components.description: Opens an unsent Outlook draft after a complete assistant response exists.
components.css: .ds-btn-draft { min-width: 132px; height: 34px; border: 1px solid ButtonBorder; border-radius: 0; background: Canvas; color: CanvasText; padding: 0 14px; font: 400 10pt system-ui, sans-serif; } .ds-btn-draft:hover { background: ButtonFace; } .ds-btn-draft:active { filter: brightness(0.96); } .ds-btn-draft:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid Highlight; outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-btn-draft:disabled { color: GrayText; opacity: 0.7; } @media (forced-colors: active) { .ds-btn-draft { forced-color-adjust: auto; } }

components.name: Toolbar Link Action
components.description: Compact borderless utility action for refreshing the selected email or opening settings.
components.css: .ds-btn-link { height: 28px; border: 0; border-radius: 0; background: Canvas; color: #005fb8; padding: 0 4px; font: 400 10pt system-ui, sans-serif; } .ds-btn-link:hover { text-decoration: underline; } .ds-btn-link:active { color: #003f7a; } .ds-btn-link:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid Highlight; outline-offset: 1px; } .ds-btn-link:disabled { color: GrayText; text-decoration: none; } @media (forced-colors: active) { .ds-btn-link { color: LinkText; forced-color-adjust: auto; } }

components.name: Composer
components.description: Multiline bounded prompt field with persistent keyboard guidance.
components.html: Ask about this email or request draft text. Ctrl+Enter sends.
components.css: .ds-composer { display: grid; gap: 4px; width: 388px; color: CanvasText; font-family: system-ui, sans-serif; } .ds-composer textarea { min-height: 72px; resize: vertical; border: 1px solid ButtonBorder; border-radius: 0; background: Canvas; color: CanvasText; padding: 4px 6px; font: 400 10pt system-ui, sans-serif; } .ds-composer textarea:hover { border-color: CanvasText; } .ds-composer textarea:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid Highlight; outline-offset: 1px; } .ds-composer textarea:disabled { background: ButtonFace; color: GrayText; } .ds-composer span { color: #505050; font: 400 8pt system-ui, sans-serif; } @media (forced-colors: active) { .ds-composer span { color: GrayText; } }

components.name: Selected Message Strip
components.description: Anchors the conversation to one visible email subject and sender without card-like elevation.
components.html: Quarterly planning follow-upFrom Alex Morgan <alex@example.test>
components.css: .ds-message-strip { display: grid; align-content: center; min-height: 52px; gap: 2px; border: 0; border-radius: 0; background: #f4f6f8; color: CanvasText; padding: 14px 18px 10px; font-family: system-ui, sans-serif; } .ds-message-strip strong { overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis; white-space: nowrap; font-size: 12pt; line-height: 1.2; } .ds-message-strip span { overflow: hidden; color: #505050; text-overflow: ellipsis; white-space: nowrap; font-size: 9pt; } .ds-message-strip:focus-within { outline: 2px solid Highlight; outline-offset: -2px; } @media (forced-colors: active) { .ds-message-strip { background: ButtonFace; } .ds-message-strip span { color: GrayText; } }

components.name: Plain-Text Transcript
components.description: Read-only conversation document with speaker labels and no chat bubbles, links, or executable output.
components.html:
Selected email loaded. Ask a question or request draft text.

You
Summarize the decision and draft a concise reply.

Assistant
Friday works for me. Please send the revised invitation.
components.css: .ds-transcript { min-height: 220px; overflow-y: auto; border: 0; border-radius: 0; background: Canvas; color: CanvasText; padding: 8px 18px; font: 400 10pt/1.4 system-ui, sans-serif; } .ds-transcript p { margin: 0 0 18px; } .ds-transcript strong { font-size: 9pt; } .ds-transcript .ds-you { color: #005fb8; } .ds-transcript .ds-system { color: #505050; font-size: 9pt; font-style: italic; } .ds-transcript:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid Highlight; outline-offset: -2px; } @media (forced-colors: active) { .ds-transcript .ds-you { color: LinkText; } .ds-transcript .ds-system { color: GrayText; } }

components.name: Draft Disclosure
components.description: Persistent disclosure that defines exactly which assistant text enters a draft.
components.html: Drafts use the entire latest assistant response.
components.css: .ds-draft-disclosure { margin: 0; background: Canvas; color: #505050; padding: 3px 18px 0; font: 400 8pt/1.3 system-ui, sans-serif; } .ds-draft-disclosure:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid Highlight; outline-offset: -2px; } @media (forced-colors: active) { .ds-draft-disclosure { color: GrayText; } }

components.name: Status Band
components.description: Plain-language operational status that confirms scope, busy state, recovery, or unsent-draft outcome.
components.html: Response received. Draft actions require your click.
components.css: .ds-status { min-height: 38px; display: flex; align-items: center; border: 0; border-radius: 0; background: #f4f6f8; color: #505050; padding: 8px 18px; font: 400 9pt/1.3 system-ui, sans-serif; } .ds-status[data-state="error"] { color: #a32626; } .ds-status:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid Highlight; outline-offset: -2px; } @media (forced-colors: active) { .ds-status { background: ButtonFace; color: GrayText; } .ds-status[data-state="error"] { color: LinkText; } }

components.name: Settings Field
components.description: Stacked native field with a visible label and accessible description.
components.css: .ds-settings-field { display: grid; gap: 4px; width: 460px; color: ButtonText; font-family: system-ui, sans-serif; } .ds-settings-field strong { font: 700 9pt system-ui, sans-serif; } .ds-settings-field input { height: 34px; border: 1px solid ButtonBorder; border-radius: 0; background: Canvas; color: CanvasText; padding: 4px 6px; font: 400 10pt system-ui, sans-serif; } .ds-settings-field input:hover { border-color: CanvasText; } .ds-settings-field input:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid Highlight; outline-offset: 1px; } .ds-settings-field span { color: #505050; font: 400 8pt system-ui, sans-serif; } @media (forced-colors: active) { .ds-settings-field span { color: GrayText; } }

narrative.overview:
Outlook Local AI Chat is a compact native Windows productivity utility. It should feel adjacent to classic Outlook, not like an AI showcase: familiar system typography, quiet white and cool-gray surfaces, square fields, restrained density, and blue reserved for direct actions.

The screen tells one ordered story: confirm which email is loaded, discuss that bounded plain-text snapshot, then deliberately open an unsent draft in Outlook. The visual hierarchy must keep this read/chat/draft-only boundary obvious. Model output is conversation content, never an executable command, and no control may imply that the utility can send mail.
keyCharacteristics: Native Windows behavior and system settings take priority over decorative identity.
One selected-message strip anchors the current scope.
A large plain-text transcript carries the work without chat bubbles or HTML treatment.
The composer and AI action are visually bounded together.
Draft actions are separate, secondary, and enabled only when usable.
Disclosure and status text state what data is used and what action occurred.

rules.name: The System Color Rule
rules.body: System canvas, text, control, highlight, and border roles outrank fixed palette values whenever Windows high contrast is active.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Blue marks direct actions and the user's transcript label. It is not decoration and must not spread into background panels or assistant content.

rules.name: The Text-Plus-State Rule
rules.body: Color never carries status alone. Every busy, error, disabled, disclosure, and draft state also has explicit text or native control state.

rules.name: The System Font Rule
rules.body: Use SystemFonts.MessageBoxFont and relative size adjustments. Do not bundle a custom font or pin typography in a way that defeats Windows text scaling.

rules.name: The Plain-Text Rule
rules.body: Transcript content is plain text only. Do not render model output as HTML, rich cards, markdown actions, links, or executable affordances.

rules.name: The Ordered Boundary Rule
rules.body: Keep message identity, conversation, composer, draft controls, and status in that order. This sequence is the interface's security explanation.

rules.name: The Transcript-Breathes Rule
rules.body: Fixed utility bands yield height to the transcript. Never shrink the conversation into a decorative card or make drafting controls compete with it.

rules.name: The Flat-Utility Rule
rules.body: App content is flat by default. Use tonal bands and native borders to separate regions, not card shadows or floating panels.

rules.name: The Native Rectangle Rule
rules.body: Keep controls square and familiar. Rounded chat bubbles, pill buttons, and oversized AI ornaments contradict the product's utility character.

dos: Do keep the selected-message identity visible before conversation content.
Do state that only the selected email is available to chat.
Do keep draft controls secondary, explicit, and disabled until a valid assistant response exists.
Do disclose that drafting uses the entire latest assistant response.
Do say "unsent draft" and "for your review" in successful draft status text.
Do inherit Windows system fonts, focus behavior, text scaling, and high-contrast colors.
Do preserve keyboard operation, including Ctrl+Enter to send, Enter to save settings, and Escape to cancel settings.
Do restore user input after request failure, timeout, cancellation, or changed-message discard when applicable.
donts: Don't add a Send Mail control, auto-send behavior, scheduling, source-message mutation, or language that implies any of those capabilities.
Don't expose model tool calls, commands, HTML, clickable output, or rich interactive response cards.
Don't hide which email is loaded or allow a response for a changed email to enter the active conversation.
Don't rely on fixed colors when Windows high contrast is active.
Don't replace native focus and disabled states with color-only signals.
Don't use chat bubbles, avatars, glowing AI motifs, gradients, rounded cards, or ornamental motion.
